For $3	ext{d}$ orbital, $n = 3$ and $l = 2$, so the value $(n + l)$ becomes $(3 + 2 = 5)$. Again, for $4	ext{s}$, $n = 4$ and $l = 0$, so the value $(n + l)$ becomes $(4 + 0 = 4)$. It shows $4	ext{s}$ orbital has lower energy than $3	ext{d}$ orbital. Therefore, the electron will first enter $4	ext{s}$ and then will go to $3	ext{d}$. Again, if the value $(n + l)$ of two orbitals are equal, then the orbital with lesser value of $n$ has lower energy and the electron will enter here first. In the same way, the orbital with higher $n$ gets the electron later for being higher in energy.

For example, the values $(n+l)$ of $3	ext{d}$ and $4	ext{p}$ are $3+2 = 5$ and $4+1 = 5$ respectively. Here in this case, since the value of $n$ in orbital $3	ext{d}$ is lesser than orbital $4	ext{p}$, so it is lower in energy and orbital $4	ext{p}$, being higher energetically will get electrons later. According to this system, the gradual sequence of energy of orbital in receiving electrons will be:

$$1	ext{s} < 2	ext{s} < 2	ext{p} < 3	ext{s} < 3	ext{p} < 4	ext{s} < 3	ext{d} < 4	ext{p} < 5	ext{s} < 4	ext{d} < 5	ext{p} < 6	ext{s} < 4	ext{f} < 5	ext{d} < 6	ext{p} < 7	ext{s} < 5	ext{f} < 6	ext{d} < 7	ext{p} < 8	ext{s}$$

We can easily remember the sequence of energy level from the chart below:

We have seen, the orbital $	ext{s}$ can contain a maximum of two electrons, the orbital $	ext{p}$ can contain a maximum of six electrons, the orbital $	ext{d}$ can contain a maximum of ten electrons and the orbital $	ext{f}$ can contain a maximum of fourteen electrons. Following this, we can configure the electrons of the following elements.

$	ext{K}(19) \rightarrow 1	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{p}^6\, 3	ext{s}^2\, 3	ext{p}^6\, 4	ext{s}^1$

$	ext{Ca}(20) \rightarrow 1	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{p}^6\, 3	ext{s}^2\, 3	ext{p}^6\, 4	ext{s}^2$

$	ext{Sc}(21) \rightarrow 1	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{p}^6\, 3	ext{s}^2\, 3	ext{p}^6\, 3	ext{d}^1\, 4	ext{s}^2$

$	ext{Ti}(22) \rightarrow 1	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{s}^2\, 2	ext{p}^6\, 3	ext{s}^2\, 3	ext{p}^6\, 3	ext{d}^2\, 4	ext{s}^2$
